name: Resurrection, Ascension, and Session

objectives.text: Retell the Easter account of the women finding the tomb empty and hearing the angel say that Jesus is risen
Recall that the risen Jesus went up into heaven while his disciples watched and that he is alive there now
Name people who saw Jesus alive after he rose, such as Mary Magdalene, Thomas, and the disciples
Describe what the risen Jesus did to show his disciples that he had a real body, such as eating fish and showing his wounds
Summarize how Jesus rose on the third day just as he and the Scriptures had said beforehand
Explain why Christians gather for worship on the first day of the week by connecting it to the day of Christ's resurrection
Explain the ascension account in Acts 1 including the angels' promise that Jesus will return in the same way
Explain that being seated at the right hand of God is biblical language for Christ's place of honor and authority rather than a description of a physical chair
List the witnesses of the risen Christ in 1 Corinthians 15 and explain why Paul appeals to living eyewitnesses
Compare the Gospel account of the empty tomb with the report that the disciples stole the body
Distinguish Christ's resurrection to glorified life that never dies again from the restoring of Lazarus to ordinary mortal life
Explain the three benefits of Christ's resurrection as the Heidelberg Catechism states them
Analyze the firstfruits imagery of 1 Corinthians 15 in light of the Old Testament harvest offering to show how the tradition sees Christ's resurrection as the pledge of believers' bodily resurrection
Interpret Psalm 110:1 and explain how the apostles apply it to Christ's ascension and session
Explain how the Reformed tradition connects Christ's session at the right hand with his continual intercession for his people
Analyze how Peter uses Psalm 16 to argue that the Old Testament anticipated the Messiah's resurrection
Trace Paul's argument about the consequences for preaching, faith, and forgiveness if Christ has not been raised
Explain from Scripture why Christ's ascension was the occasion for his pouring out of the Holy Spirit
Explain how Ephesians presents the seated Christ as ruling over all things for the sake of the church
Explain the continuity and transformation of Christ's risen body as the tradition confesses it, the same body now glorified
Compare the Reformed teaching that Christ's human nature is now in heaven with the Lutheran teaching on the ubiquity of his body
Construct a historical case for the resurrection from the burial, the empty tomb, the appearances, and the rise of the early church's proclamation
Evaluate naturalistic theories such as the swoon, hallucination, and wrong tomb theories against the biblical and historical evidence
Explain how Paul grounds the believer's union with the risen and ascended Christ and the call to seek the things above in Christ's session

changes: Kept and sharpened the real competencies (empty tomb, ascension account, Psalm 110 and session, intercession, firstfruits, the historical case, naturalistic theories, rule from the right hand). Reworded the faith-application objective so students explain the tradition's teaching rather than apply it personally. Folded the 'Jesus is alive and reigning' item into the early ascension objective. Dropped the closing synthesis of exaltation because it belongs to the States of Humiliation and Exaltation sibling. Added objectives on the eyewitnesses, Christ's real and glorified body, the Lord's Day, the benefits in Heidelberg Q45, resurrection versus resuscitation, Psalm 16 in Acts 2, Paul's argument in 1 Corinthians 15:12-19, the ascension and Pentecost, the location of Christ's human nature, and union with the ascended Christ. Updated the anchors to verse-specific passages and to the matching Heidelberg and Westminster articles.
